Derivation: Ael young/growing + -in individual participant.

HEADWORD: Aen
================================================================
Pronunciation: /ah-ehn/

USE 1: Verb
Meaning: Speak / Tell / Breathe
Usage note: Formal/poetic use: deeper or ritual speaking. Use in rituals, court, formal address, writing, and when emphasizing depth. Combine with Li- / -en.

USE 2: Conjunction
Meaning: That

USE 3: Suffix
Meaning: -aen (verb-forming)

USE 4: Noun
Meaning: Breath of Life

Available example count: 61
Example 1:
  Celan: aen serathrin ser khumrel.
  English: The confidant speaks with compassion.
Example 2:
  Celan: aen thar lian.
  English: The heart speaks truth.
Example 3:
  Celan: ver aen I unar kelka.
  English: I do not speak one word.
Example 4:
  Celan: aen kalrin kalkel.
  English: The sovereign speaks a decree.
Example 5:
  Celan: elan, va aen lian!
  English: Well then, speak the truth!
Related words: Aenaen; Aenor; Aenvor
Source entry IDs: LX-V2-0028; LX-V2-0062; LX-V3-0009; LX-V4-0102; DM-RM-V3-0005

================================================================
HEADWORD: Belshara
================================================================
Pronunciation: /bel-shah-rah/

USE 1: Noun
Meaning: Coordinated Maneuver / Formation Movement / Tactical Path. Refers to moving troops in a specific, planned way.
Usage note: Bel (bind/weave) + Shara (path/journey)

USE 2: Noun
Meaning: Duty (Bound Path)
Usage note: Bel (bind) + Shara (path)

USE 3: Modal
Meaning: Necessity (Must/Have to)
Usage note: "on a bound path"

USE 4: Noun
Meaning: Necessity / Obligation

Root families: BEL; SHARA
Available example count: 5
Example 1:
  Celan: lorin belshara Ilin shan vethor.
  English: Duty guides us through the shadow.
Example 2:
  Celan: Var I belshara.
  English: I must go.
Example 3:
  Celan: Rinaen belshara an Ilin.
  English: Duty is with us.
Example 4:
  Celan: Var I an phelvin. Rinaen kelvor-ian kadreneth. Rinaen belshara.
  English: Proceeding to acquire a beverage. My mouth is dry. Hydration is a necessity.
Example 5:
  Celan: mbaen an I nor-ka belshara.
  English: I need help; I must be helped.
Related words: Bel; Shara; Bel-; Shara-; Belar; Awekshara; Beldava; Brosshara; Belkes; Dralshara; Belkor; Droshara; Belkoraen; Emilshara; Belkren; Felshara; Belmek; Kasharaen; Belmor; Kinnshara; Belnoraen; Lorshara; Belor; Mekshara; Belpralmek; Morlshara; Belraku; Nakshara; Belreth; Rakushara; Belrin; Rethshara; Belrinpel; Sharaen; Belshan; Sharaka; Belshen; Sharalorin; Belsura; Sharashen; Belthal; Sharavok; Belvekaen; Sharbel; Belvelrathor; Tharshara; Belverd; Tharsharaen; Belvethral; Vershara; Belvok; Weksharaen; Belwek; Zhelshara; Belxar; Zhirshara; Belzhir; Belzhirkavor; Belzhirvek; Belzor; Belzoraen; Dralbelaen; Drobel; Emilbel; Lianbel; Lorbel; Nyelbel; Rinbel; Shenbel; Thaenbel; Thalbel; Tharbel; Varbelor; Verdbel; Vethbel; Zhelbel; Zhirbel

  English: The gate is illusory and the guard is under compulsion.

  English: The guard is under compulsion; the enemy compels them toward the gate.

  English: The enemy compels the guard; the practitioner releases them from the compulsion.

  English: The practitioner releases the guard from compulsion and detects a perceptual veil at the gate.
